class Notification::PushMessage
  include NotificationsHelper
  include Rails.application.routes.url_helpers

  def initialize(notification)
    @notification = notification
  end

  def to_h
    {
      title: title,
      body: body,
      url: url,
      badge: badge
    }
  end

  private
    attr_reader :notification

    def title
      case notification.source
      when Event
        event_notification_title(notification.source)
      when Mention
        "#{notification.source.mentioner.first_name} @mentioned you"
      end
    end

    def body
      case notification.source
      when Event
        event_notification_body(notification.source)
      when Mention
        notification.source.source.mentionable_content.truncate(200)
      end
    end

    def url
      polymorphic_path(notification, script_name: notification.account.slug, only_path: true)
    end

    def badge
      notification.user.notifications.unread.count
    end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/notification/pushing.rb
module Notification::Pushing
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :push_later
    after_update_commit :push_later, if: -> { source_id_previously_changed? || source_type_previously_changed? }
  end

  def push_later
    Notification::PushJob.perform_later(self) if should_push?
  end

  def push_now
    return unless should_push? && Push.vapid_configured?
    return if source.nil? || card.nil?

    payload = Notification::PushMessage.new(self).to_h

    user.push_subscriptions.find_each do |subscription|
      subscription.notification(**payload)
    end
  end

  private
    def should_push?
      !read? && account.active? && user.active? && !user.system? && user.push_subscriptions.exists?
    end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/jobs/notification/push_job.rb
class Notification::PushJob < ApplicationJob
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  retry_on WebPush::TooManyRequests, WebPush::PushServiceError, Net::OpenTimeout, Net::ReadTimeout,
    wait: :polynomially_longer, attempts: 3

  def perform(notification)
    notification.push_now
  end
end
EOF

class Users::PushSubscriptionsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_user
  before_action :ensure_current_user

  def create
    subscription = @user.push_subscriptions.find_or_initialize_by(endpoint: push_subscription_params[:endpoint])

    if subscription.update(push_subscription_params)
      render json: { id: subscription.id }, status: :created
    else
      render json: subscription.errors, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  def destroy
    @user.push_subscriptions.find(params[:id]).destroy!
    head :no_content
  end

  private
    def set_user
      @user = Current.account.users.active.find(params[:user_id])
    end

    def ensure_current_user

    assert_equal @subscription.p256dh_key, delivered[:p256dh]

messages.thinking:
**A Deep Dive into Rails Callbacks and Testing Gotchas**

Okay, here's what I've just figured out. This is why step-by-step debugging is invaluable.

First, I was puzzled why `Notification::PushJob` didn't enqueue during the `Notification::PushingTest`, even though the `Turbo::Streams::ActionBroadcastJob` did. I went through the code in `app/models/notification.rb` and noticed the callbacks. Then, it hit me: the transaction in `ActiveRecord` tests should *allow* those callbacks to fire! So, it had to be a different issue. I checked the account and user statuses, the existence of subscriptions – all seemed correct.

The issue was right in `app/models/notification/pushing.rb`. I reviewed the class, specifically the `included do` block with the `after_create_commit` and `after_update_commit` callbacks. That's when it clicked! The shared method name, `:push_later`, in *both* `after_create_commit` and `after_update_commit`, was the culprit! It's that classic Rails gotcha. Rails uses the method name as a callback identifier, and the second one overwrites the first! It's a fundamental misunderstanding of how the callbacks are registered and handled, especially with the same method name.

The fix? We have to treat each `after_commit` callback as unique to its situation. Either we need to use `after_commit :push_later, on: :create` + `after_commit :push_on_update, on: :update`, or use a lambda, or combine both calls in the same method.

Next, I looked at the errors in `Push::SubscriptionTest`. It was a simple `Net::HTTPGone` object. When a `WebPush::ResponseError` is initialized, it calls `@response.body`, which leads to an `IOError` if the response doesn't have a proper body, especially when stubbed. The quick fix is to either stub the HTTP response to have a body in testing, or to ensure that the response object is set correctly.

I've got the fixes ready: I'll tweak `app/models/notification/pushing.rb` and `test/models/push/subscription_test.rb` and re-run the tests. Hopefully, all will be green this time!

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/notification/pushing.rb
module Notification::Pushing
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit -> { push_later }
    after_update_commit -> { push_later }, if: -> { source_id_previously_changed? || source_type_previously_changed? }
  end

  def push_later
    Notification::PushJob.perform_later(self) if should_push?
  end

  def push_now
    return unless should_push? && Push.vapid_configured?
    return if source.nil? || card.nil?

    payload = Notification::PushMessage.new(self).to_h

    user.push_subscriptions.find_each do |subscription|
      subscription.notification(**payload)
    end
  end

  private
    def should_push?
      !read? && account.active? && user.active? && !user.system? && user.push_subscriptions.exists?
    end
end
EOF

**My Analysis of Fizzy's Notification Pushing Logic**

Okay, so I'm digging into Fizzy's notification system. My initial observation is that every URL within Fizzy, regardless of whether it's single-tenant or multi-tenant, seems to rely on `account.slug` using `/#{external_account_id}`. That seems like a pretty standard practice, but it's always worth confirming.

Now, the real question is around `Notification::Pushing`, specifically when a `Notification` gets re-triggered after being marked as read. Let's trace it through `Notifier#notify`. If the `notification` isn't brand new, it calls `source_type_will_change!` and then `update!`. Critically, that `update!` call sets `read_at: nil` if it was previously set and changes the `source` field.

This is where it gets interesting: the `after_update_commit` callback triggers. Here, if the `source_id` has changed and the notification is no longer marked as read (because `read_at` was set to `nil` in the previous step), it calls `push_later`.

The key discrepancy here is when `Notification` is updated through `notification.read` or `notification.unread`. In this flow, `source_id_previously_changed?` and `source_type_previously_changed?` are both `false`, so `push_later` *doesn't* get called. This is the behavior I want to isolate and verify.

To nail this down, I'm going to create an end-to-end test in `test/models/notification/pushing_test.rb` that covers the full `Notifier` -> `Card` -> `Comment` flow, as well as the specific "read-then-new-event" scenario. Once that's in place, I will run the entire test suite, rubocop, and Brakeman to ensure the change behaves as expected and does not impact any other functionality. This is a critical edge case, so I need to be thorough.
